items.title: Tesla Reportedly Begins New Optimus Supplier Audits in China
items.summary: Chinese media reported that Tesla initiated new supplier audits for Optimus components in Ningbo on September 17, with component orders already placed. These audits focused on manufacturing consistency and equipment commissioning as preparation for robot production. Supplier representatives confirmed cooperation with Tesla on related robotics projects but did not explicitly confirm the latest audit visits. These developments suggest progress in the supply chain alongside factory construction, though no new production timetable was established. The audits represent a preparatory step toward realizing potential robot output.

items.title: Video Friday: Two Birotors Make a Quadrotor
items.summary: A quadrotor is described as being composed of two birotors that interact with each other. NYU Tandon researchers developed an undulatory robot that uses water to achieve traction and successfully climb inclines and clear steps. Kubi 2.0 is a desktop telepresence AI robot designed for remote interaction and physical AI agent engagement. An underwater quadruped robot was designed to enable amphibious mobility, featuring custom waterproof motor housings. Other advancements include semi-humanoid robots, robotic optics labs, and AI systems for ecosystem support.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Two Birotors Make a Quadrotor". This report details the development of an undulatory robot utilizing water for traction to successfully ascend inclines and clear steps. NYU Tandon researchers engineered a system that employs water dynamics to generate the necessary force for climbing and overcoming obstacles. The research involved designing a robot that interacts with the aquatic medium to achieve locomotion, demonstrating the viability of fluid-based propulsion for climbing applications. Other related developments include the Kubi 2.0 desktop telepresence AI robot and an underwater quadruped robot featuring custom waterproof motor housings. These advancements highlight progress in amphibious robotics and sophisticated AI agent engagement systems. The ongoing research indicates further potential for novel locomotion methods in robotics and artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: D-Robotics at ROSCon Global 2026 — Let’s Connect in Toronto
items.summary: The D-Robotics team will be at ROSCon Global 2026 in Toronto from September 22–24 to connect with the robotics community. ROS 2 is central to the RDK robotics development experience, which supports multiple ROS 2 distributions. TogetheROS.Bot utilizes ROS 2 with hardware-accelerated capabilities for robotics. D-Robotics will showcase an RDK X5 × Piper demo at the AgileX Robotics booth, demonstrating on-device perception and AI inference. They will also be present at the LooperRobotics booth to discuss spatial AI applications.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: D-Robotics at ROSCon Global 2026 — Let’s Connect in Toronto" reports on the presence of the D-Robotics team at the upcoming ROSCon Global 2026 event in Toronto. The team will be connecting with the robotics community to showcase advancements in robotics development. The D-Robotics group will exhibit an RDK X5 by Piper demonstration at the AgileX Robotics booth to illustrate on-device perception and artificial intelligence inference capabilities. Furthermore, the team will engage with the LooperRobotics booth to discuss spatial artificial intelligence applications, leveraging the foundation of ROS 2 and the TogetheROS.Bot framework which incorporates hardware-accelerated capabilities. This presence signals continued development in integrated on-device AI and spatial reasoning within the broader robotics ecosystem.
